brief: Goldman's Friday Mark to Market: a tech-led selloff drove US equities to their worst week since April 2025's Liberation Day, with the S&P down 370bps to 6910, Nasdaq -561bps to 25028, Russell -276bps to 2581, breadth 15:1 negative, all 11 sectors red, and GS's AI Semis, Data Center and Retail Favorites baskets each down double digits on the week; NVDA fell 14% on reports the SEC opened an accounting probe. That news intensified a flight-to-quality bid: rates rallied across the curve, vols hit three-week highs, and the market repriced the Fed's path to 22bps of December hikes with a 60bps peak by mid-2027. Credit closed softer (CDX IG wider, CDX HY lower, the 30y hyperscaler credit basket at YTD wides), while real money was less active and fast money bought protection. The dollar rallied broadly except against safe havens JPY and CHF, with USDJPY on a 158 handle on the US yield drop. GS still favors USD longs with lighter risk and tight stops, added CAD shorts to its EUR/CHF short bias, likes JPY longs, and argues the dollar's path of least resistance stays higher on inflows despite its growing negative beta to equities.
